name: hotplug_tests
prose: Precondition: nb_available_cpus, tos_resident_cpu and the CPU topology are initialised. Behaviour: it allocates a cpumask (returning -ENOMEM at once if that fails), builds the CPU groups with alloc_init_cpu_groups (on a negative result it frees the cpumask and returns -ENOMEM, not the helper's error value) and allocates one page buffer (on failure it frees the groups and the cpumask and returns -ENOMEM). Otherwise it calls down_and_up_cpus on cpu_online_mask, then on each CPU group (printing the group's CPU list), adding the returned numbers of unexpected errors, frees the page buffer, the groups and the cpumask, and returns the accumulated error count (0 when nothing unexpected happened). The first call's count is assigned to err and each group's count is added to it.
note: psci_checker.c:186-229. Contract left empty because of the errno return and the global state it reads.

name: TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_request,
prose: Generated function trace_scm_smc_request(a0, smc), a static inline expanded from TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_request, ...). It returns nothing; when the scm_smc_request tracepoint is enabled it calls the registered probes with a0 and smc, and does nothing otherwise. smc must point to an arm_smccc_args. The probe's record fill (not this wrapper) stores smc_id = a0, svc_id = (args[0] >> 8) & 0xFF, cmd_id = args[0] & 0xFF, args_cnt = min(args[1] & 0xF, 6) and copies that many words from args[2] onward into a dynamic array.
note: qcom_scm_trace.h:13-43. Old prose attributed the record fill to the wrapper; it is done by the probe's TP_fast_assign.

name: TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_done,
prose: Generated function trace_scm_smc_done(ret, smc_id, smc_res), a static inline expanded from TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_done, ...). It returns nothing; when the tracepoint is enabled it calls the registered probes with its arguments, and does nothing otherwise. smc_res must point to an arm_smccc_res. The probe's record fill stores ret, smc_id and smc_res->a0 to a3 (as res, res0, res1, res2).
note: qcom_scm_trace.h:89-111.

name: sysfb_unregister
prose: Precondition: the caller serialises access to the file-level pd (sysfb_disable and sysfb_init hold disable_lock). Behaviour: returns false without changing anything if pd is NULL or an error pointer. Otherwise it calls platform_device_unregister(pd), sets pd to NULL and returns true.
note: sysfb.c:44-53.

name: sysfb_disable
prose: Precondition: may sleep; dev may be NULL. Behaviour: it takes disable_lock and calls sysfb_parent_dev(&screen_info), which returns the PCI device that owns the screen_info framebuffer (with a device reference held), NULL if there is none, or an error pointer. If dev is NULL, or the parent is NULL, or dev equals the parent, it calls sysfb_unregister and sets disabled to true; an error pointer is neither NULL nor equal to a device, so with a non-NULL dev it changes nothing. It releases disable_lock and returns nothing. It never drops the reference that sysfb_parent_dev took on a valid parent, so that reference is left held.
note: checked sysfb.c:67-79 and sysfb_parent_dev (124-140). Old prose matches; the error-pointer case is now stated.

name: sysfb_handles_screen_info
prose: Precondition: none. Behaviour: returns true when screen_info_video_type(&screen_info) is nonzero and false otherwise; it only reads the global screen_info and takes no lock or reference.
note: sysfb.c:93-98.

name: sysfb_init
prose: Precondition: runs as an __init initcall and may sleep. Behaviour: it applies screen_info fixups, takes disable_lock and, if sysfb is already disabled, returns 0 without registering anything. Otherwise it applies the EFI quirks and looks up the parent with sysfb_parent_dev; if that returns an error pointer it returns the error with nothing registered and no parent reference held. Then, if sysfb_parse_mode reports a simple-framebuffer compatible mode, it tries sysfb_create_simplefb into pd and, if that succeeds, goes to put_device. Otherwise it picks a legacy name by video type (ega-, vga-, vesa-, efi-framebuffer, else platform-framebuffer), allocates the platform device (-ENOMEM on failure), sets its parent to the looked-up device, sets the efifb fwnode, adds the screen_info as platform data and calls platform_device_add; if the data or add call fails it calls platform_device_put (leaving the pd pointer set to that device) and returns the error. In every path after the lookup it calls put_device(parent) (a no-op for NULL), releases disable_lock and returns the result (0 on success).
note: checked sysfb.c:142-221. Reviewer round 1 RIGHT (simplefb failure falls back to the legacy device). Added the pd pointer being left as is after platform_device_put on the error paths (lines 214-215).

name: tegra_ivc_total_queue_size
prose: Precondition: queue_size is an unsigned int; the sum with the header size must not wrap if the result is to be meaningful. Behaviour: it returns 0 after logging an error that includes the function name, queue_size and the required alignment if queue_size is not a multiple of TEGRA_IVC_ALIGN (64); otherwise it returns queue_size + sizeof(struct tegra_ivc_header), which is 128 (two 64-byte unions: tx and rx). It has no other effects.
contract: /*@ requires queue_size <= 4294967167; ensures ((queue_size % 64 != 0) ==> result == 0) && ((queue_size % 64 == 0) ==> result == queue_size + 128); */
note: checked ivc.c:53-70 (struct size 2 x TEGRA_IVC_ALIGN = 128) and 562-571. Old prose and contract said the header is 64 bytes, which was wrong; the contract only describes the return value, the error log is the only other effect.

name: tf_prepare_idle
prose: Precondition: none; mode is an unsigned long. Behaviour: for TF_PM_MODE_LP0, LP1, LP1_NO_MC_CLK, LP2 and LP2_NOFLUSH_L2 it calls tf_generic_smc(TF_CPU_PM, <the matching TF_CPU_PM_S* code>, cpu_boot_addr); for TF_PM_MODE_NONE it issues no SMC. For each of those six modes it then sets the global tf_idle_mode to mode and returns 0. For any other mode it issues no SMC, leaves tf_idle_mode unchanged and returns -EINVAL.
note: trusted_foundations.c:65-100. Contract left empty because it writes a global and returns an errno.

name: altera_cvp_write
prose: Precondition: mgr->priv is the altera_cvp_conf with a nonzero priv->block_size, buf holds count readable bytes and is accessed as 32-bit words (so it should be 4-byte aligned), and the CVP write init succeeded. Behaviour: it sends count bytes in blocks of min(block_size, remaining) using altera_cvp_send_block, incrementing conf->sent_packets once per block. Before each block, if priv->wait_credit exists it calls it with the bytes sent so far and returns its nonzero status at once (the data sent so far stays sent, fewer than count bytes). When altera_cvp_chkcfg is set and the bytes sent so far are a multiple of 4 KiB after a block, it calls altera_cvp_chk_error and returns the status if it is negative (nonnegative values are ignored). After all blocks it returns 0 if altera_cvp_chkcfg is clear, or the result of altera_cvp_chk_error(mgr, count) if it is set.
note: altera-cvp.c:432-483. Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 RIGHT (early wait_credit return, short final block, u32 access of buf).

name: feature_id
prose: Precondition: none; value is a 64-bit DFH register value. Behaviour: it extracts DFH_ID (bits 11:0) and DFH_TYPE (bits 63:60) and returns FEATURE_ID_FIU_HEADER (0xfe) when the type is DFH_TYPE_FIU (4), the 12-bit ID when the type is DFH_TYPE_PRIVATE (3), and FEATURE_ID_AFU (0xff) when the type is DFH_TYPE_AFU (1). For any other type it executes WARN_ON(1) and returns 0.
note: dfl.c:966-980 and dfl.h:72-82. Old prose had the wrong constants (FIU is type 4 and ID 0xfe, AFU is 0xff); all three reviewer notes about the constants were RIGHT.

name: i2cr_get_command
prose: Precondition: address fits in 31 bits (it is shifted left by one in 32-bit arithmetic); parity is a bool. Behaviour: it shifts address left by one, then calls i2cr_check_parity32 on the shifted value with parity as the starting value, which toggles that bool once for every set bit of the shifted value; if the result is true it sets bit 0 of the shifted value. It returns that value. The returned word's population count has the same parity as the starting parity value.
note: fsi-master-i2cr.c:39-72. Contract states only the shift (true); the parity bit is described in the prose.

name: fsi_occ_submit
prose: Precondition: request holds at least req_len bytes (req_len at least 2), response holds at least *resp_len bytes, resp_len is non-NULL. Behaviour: it first sets *resp_len to 0; then returns -ENODEV without locking if dev has no OCC driver data and -EINVAL without locking if the caller's response size was below 7. It checksums the request, takes occ->occ_lock interruptibly (returning that error on failure), sets occ->client_buffer to response, client_buffer_size to the caller's size and client_response_size to 0, and returns -ENOENT via done if occ->buffer is NULL. It allocates a sequence number, writes the request to SRAM (occ_putsram), triggers the attention (occ_trigger_attn) and polls the response header with occ_getsram until the response is ready (-ETIMEDOUT after OCC_TIMEOUT_MS), failing with the error of any SRAM access; it returns -EMSGSIZE if the response data length + 7 exceeds the caller's size, re-reads the whole response when the data length is above 1, and verifies the checksum with occ_verify_checksum (its error is returned). On success it stores data length + 7 in client_response_size. At done it sets *resp_len to occ->client_response_size (0 unless the response was verified) and releases occ->occ_lock, returning the result.
note: checked fsi-occ.c:465-599. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (*resp_len comes from occ->client_response_size, set at line 592/505, and is zeroed up front); round 2 RIGHT (NULL occ->buffer returns -ENOENT).

name: cs5535_gpio_set_irq
prose: Precondition: group and irq are unsigned ints. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL without touching hardware if group > 7 or irq > 15. Otherwise it reads MSR_PIC_ZSEL_HIGH with rdmsr, replaces the 4-bit field of the low word at bit position group * 4 with irq (the upper word is written back unchanged) and writes the MSR with wrmsr, returning 0.
note: gpio-cs5535.c:148-162. Contract left empty because it accesses an MSR and returns an errno.

name: sprd_pmic_eic_toggle_trigger
prose: Precondition: chip is the PMIC EIC gpio_chip and offset a line number. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It reads the irq's trigger type and, if neither the rising nor the falling edge bit (IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH mask) is set, returns without touching any register. Otherwise it reads the EIC data bit with sprd_pmic_eic_get (0, 1 or a negative regmap error), then loops: if the value is nonzero (including a negative error) it writes IEV to 0, else to 1; it re-reads the data bit and, if the new value differs from the previous one, logs a warning, adopts the new value and repeats the write. When two consecutive reads agree it sets the IE bit and then the TRIG bit of the line to 1. The return values of the register updates are ignored; the loop is unbounded while the input keeps changing.
note: gpio-pmic-eic-sprd.c:233-260. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the IE and TRIG updates are at lines 257-259; round 2 RIGHT (get can return a negative error); the old prose said the early return happens when IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH is not included, but the test is whether either edge bit is set.

name: gpiod_direction_output_nonotify
prose: Precondition: desc is a valid GPIO descriptor. Behaviour: it normalises value (inverting it if GPIOD_FLAG_ACTIVE_LOW is set, else !!value). It returns -EIO if the line is used as an enabled IRQ. If GPIOD_FLAG_OPEN_DRAIN is set it tries gpio_set_config(PIN_CONFIG_DRIVE_OPEN_DRAIN); if that succeeds it goes to set_output_value; otherwise, if the value is high, it emulates open drain by calling gpiod_direction_input_nonotify and, on success, setting GPIOD_FLAG_IS_OUT and returning 0 (returning the input call's error if it fails); if the value is low it falls through to set_output_value. Open source is symmetric (emulated by switching to input when the value is low). With neither flag it calls gpio_set_config(PIN_CONFIG_DRIVE_PUSH_PULL) and ignores its result. At set_output_value it calls gpio_set_bias, returning its error, and then returns the result of gpiod_direction_output_raw_commit, which returns -ENODEV if the chip guard cannot be obtained, -EIO if the chip has neither set() nor direction_output() or if it has no direction_output() and reports a non-output direction, the negative error of get_direction/direction_output/set (a positive callback result becomes -EBADE), and otherwise 0 with GPIOD_FLAG_IS_OUT set. gpio_set_config errors are never returned.
note: checked gpiolib.c:3008-3066, 2901-2953, 2793-2808, 2885-2899, 2722-2751. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the emulation path does call gpiod_direction_input_nonotify and return its error (3054-3057); rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT (config errors are not propagated; no -EOPNOTSUPP is reachable through the guards).

name: amdgpu_acpi_enumerate_xcc
prose: Precondition: none; it initialises the globals itself. Behaviour: it initialises amdgpu_acpi_dev_list and numa_info_xa, then for each id below AMD_XCC_MAX_HID looks up the ACPI device with HID "AMD<AMD_XCC_HID_START + id>"; at the first id with no device it stops (the loop ends, returning 0). For a found device it kzallocs an amdgpu_acpi_xcc_info; if that fails it logs, drops the ACPI device reference and returns -ENOMEM (nothing to free). Otherwise it stores the ACPI handle, drops the device reference, and calls amdgpu_acpi_get_xcc_info; on failure it frees the xcc_info and goes on to the next id. It then gets the existing device info for the returned sbdf, or creates one with amdgpu_acpi_dev_init if none exists; if amdgpu_acpi_dev_init returns -ENOMEM it frees the xcc_info and returns -ENOMEM; if no dev_info results (another failure) it frees the xcc_info and continues. Otherwise it appends the xcc_info to dev_info->xcc_list. It returns 0 after the loop. Earlier attachments are kept when an -ENOMEM return happens.
note: checked amdgpu_acpi.c:1093-1154. Matches the old prose; reviewer round 2 claim (nothing to free on kzalloc failure) is consistent with line 1119-1123. Contract left empty because the prose names -ENOMEM and the function writes globals.

name: trap_mask_map_hw_to_sw
prose: Precondition: none; mask is a 32-bit SPI_GDBG_PER_VMID_CNTL register value. Behaviour: a pure function. It returns the EXCP_EN field of mask (bits 12:4, shifted down to bits 8:0), with KFD_DBG_TRAP_MASK_TRAP_ON_WAVE_START (1 << 30) added when TRAP_ON_START (bit 14) is set and KFD_DBG_TRAP_MASK_TRAP_ON_WAVE_END (1 << 31) added when TRAP_ON_END (bit 15) is set. It reads no other state.
note: amdgpu_amdkfd_gfx_v12.c:261-272; field positions in gc_12_0_0_sh_mask.h:27240-27250 (EXCP_EN mask 0x1FF0, TRAP_ON_START 0x4000, TRAP_ON_END 0x8000) and include/uapi/linux/kfd_ioctl.h:925-926. All three old claims (mask & 0x3FF, bits 8/9) were wrong.

name: amdgpu_amdkfd_gpuvm_alloc_memory_of_gpu
prose: Precondition: adev and drm_priv are valid, mem is writable, offset may be NULL, flags select VRAM, GTT, or (otherwise) a CPU-domain allocation. Behaviour: with VRAM set it allocates in VRAM (or GTT when adev->apu_prefer_gtt is set); with GTT in GTT; otherwise the domain is CPU/GTT and flags must request USERPTR (returns -EINVAL if offset is NULL or *offset is 0) or DOORBELL/MMIO_REMAP (returns -EINVAL if size > UINT_MAX, -ENOMEM if the sg table cannot be created, using *offset as the address) or it returns -EINVAL. It kzallocs *mem (-ENOMEM via the err label if that fails), halves size for an AQL queue and returns -EINVAL (after the unwind) if the page-aligned size is 0. It reserves the memory limit (error returned after unwinding), creates the GEM object (error returned after unreserving the limit), allows the vma node for drm_priv, creates the GEM handle (those two failures unwind without an explicit unreserve, since dropping the GEM object frees the BO), fills in the kgd_mem (BO, va, domain, process_info) and adds it to the process BO list. For USERPTR it calls init_user_pages; for DOORBELL/MMIO_REMAP it pins the BO to GTT; otherwise, if the process has an unsignalled eviction fence, it validates the BO against it. Failures of those three steps remove the mem from the list, delete the GEM handle, revoke the vma node and then drop the GEM object reference (which frees the kgd_mem) or kfree *mem, free the sync object and the sg table; the error is returned and *mem is left dangling. On success it stores amdgpu_bo_mmap_offset(bo) in *offset if offset is non-NULL and returns 0.
note: checked amdgpu_amdkfd_gpuvm.c:1691-1889 (slice cut the head). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: drm_vma_node_allow and drm_gem_handle_create failures go to err_reserve_limit (line 1872) without unreserving the limit.

name: amdgpu_bo_list_ioctl
prose: Precondition: filp->driver_priv is the amdgpu_fpriv and data is a writable drm_amdgpu_bo_list. Behaviour: for every operation it first calls amdgpu_bo_create_list_entry_array on args->in (copying bo_number entries of bo_info_size bytes from bo_info_ptr), returning its error (-EINVAL for too many entries, -ENOMEM, -EFAULT or the memdup error) with *args untouched. CREATE builds a list with amdgpu_bo_list_create and allocates a handle with idr_alloc under bo_list_lock; a negative idr_alloc result puts the new list and returns it. DESTROY calls amdgpu_bo_list_destroy(fpriv, handle) and sets the output handle to 0 (success is returned whether or not that handle existed). UPDATE builds a list and swaps it in with idr_replace; an error pointer from idr_replace puts the new list and returns PTR_ERR(old), otherwise the old list is put. Any other operation returns -EINVAL. On every failure the info array is freed with kvfree, a just-created list is put and *args is not modified. On success it zeroes *args, stores the handle in args->out.list_handle, frees info and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; function is amdgpu_bo_list.c:223-295. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: DESTROY does not report a missing handle (the destroy helper returns void). The old prose also named the wrong input field (bo_info_ptr, not bo_list_ptr).

name: amdgpu_connector_dvi_detect
prose: Precondition: connector is an amdgpu DVI/HDMI-family connector, force requests forced detection, and the caller holds no runtime PM reference. Behaviour: unless running in the kms poll worker it takes a runtime PM reference with pm_runtime_get_sync; if that fails it calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns connector_status_disconnected immediately (no mark_last_busy, no scratch register update). If detected_hpd_without_ddc was set it clears it and forces detection. If not forced and amdgpu_connector_check_hpd_status_unchanged says so, it returns connector->status (through exit). If a ddc_bus exists it probes DDC; if the probe fails, force is false and HPD is sensed, it sets detected_hpd_without_ddc, schedules the hotplug work for one second later and returns the initial connector_status_disconnected through exit (without updating the scratch registers). If the probe succeeded it frees and re-reads the EDID: no EDID gives connector_status_connected with broken_edid set; a digital EDID gives connected and sets use_digital; an analog EDID on a shared DDC line gives disconnected (after freeing the EDID); amdgpu_connector_shared_ddc may then adjust the status. If connected and digital, or for DVI-D and HDMI-A connectors, it goes to out; if not forced it goes to out, returning connector->status when the last detection was by load (otherwise the current ret); if forced and dac_load_detect is set it asks the first DAC/TVDAC encoder with a detect hook: with a valid EDID result and status not connected it uses the encoder's detect result and updates use_digital and detected_by_load; with a broken EDID it only updates use_digital and keeps ret. At out it calls amdgpu_connector_update_scratch_regs(connector, ret). Unless in the poll worker it then marks the device last busy and puts the autosuspend reference, and returns ret.
note: slice cut the head; function is amdgpu_connectors.c:1011-1155. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (pm_runtime_get_sync failure path returns before mark_last_busy and the scratch update, lines 1024-1027).

name: amdgpu_device_reinit_after_reset
prose: Precondition: reset_context is valid. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if reset_context->reset_device_list is NULL. Otherwise it computes full_reset and init_level (AMDGPU_INIT_LEVEL_DEFAULT for AMD_RESET_METHOD_ON_INIT, AMDGPU_INIT_LEVEL_RESET_RECOVERY otherwise), sets r to 0 and, for each device in the list, sets its init level. If full_reset is set it clears the DPC status and RAS error state and calls amdgpu_device_asic_init; if that fails it only logs and r keeps the error. If it succeeds it runs ip resume phase 1 (failure jumps to out), checks VRAM loss, creates a coredump unless AMDGPU_SKIP_COREDUMP is set, increments the VRAM-lost counter if lost, then calls amdgpu_device_fw_loading (on failure it returns that error immediately, without setting asic_reset_res), restores the XCP partition mode, runs resume phase 2, enables the TTM buffer functions if the ring is ready, runs phase 3, fills the reset magic if VRAM was lost, registers the GPU instance, adds an XGMI device for a standalone multi-node GPU, runs late init, resumes the DRM client, resumes RAS (a device in RMA state gives r = -EINVAL), and updates the XGMI topology if a hive exists (its result becomes r). Any of those failures jumps to out with r set; at out, if r is 0 it sets the init level to DEFAULT, runs the IRQ reset-resume helper and the IB ring tests (a failing test sets r to -EAGAIN and returns -EAGAIN immediately); if r is nonzero it stores r in tmp_adev->asic_reset_res and continues with the next device. With full_reset clear the phases are skipped and every device goes through the r == 0 branch. The final return value is r from the last processed device (0 if it succeeded), so errors of earlier devices are overwritten, apart from the immediate -EAGAIN return.
note: checked amdgpu_device.c:5999-6136. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (VRAM-lost check, coredump and counter come before fw_loading, lines 6039-6051); round 2 RIGHT (loop continues and the later device overwrites r; non-full reset also runs the IRQ helper and ring tests).

name: amdgpu_discovery_set_ip_blocks
prose: Precondition: adev is a valid amdgpu_device. Behaviour: for the legacy ASICs (Vega10/12/20, Raven, Arcturus, Aldebaran and Cyan Skillfish without the SKILLFISH2 flag) it calls amdgpu_discovery_init (failure is ignored), the ASIC's reg_base_init and fills in ip_versions and counts; for Cyan Skillfish2 it runs amdgpu_discovery_reg_base_init and returns -EINVAL if that fails, then the harvest/gfx/mall/vcn info helpers; for any other ASIC it runs amdgpu_discovery_reg_base_init and returns its error (after drm_err) if it fails, then the same info helpers. It then initialises the SoC config and sysfs, sets adev->family from the GC IP version (returning -EINVAL for an unknown version, and setting AMD_APU_IS_VANGOGH in apu_flags for 10.3.1), sets AMD_IS_APU for the APU GC versions and for SMUIO 13.0.3/13.0.11 when get_pkg_type reports AMDGPU_PKG_TYPE_APU, and assigns the nbio, hdp, df, smuio and lsdma function tables by IP version (left unchanged for unrecognised versions). It then registers IP blocks in this order, returning the error of the first failing helper: common, GMC; for SR-IOV VFs PSP then IH; otherwise IH and, when the firmware load type is PSP, PSP; SMU when the load type is PSP; display; GC; SDMA; SMU again when the load type is DIRECT (not SR-IOV VF) or RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO with amdgpu_dpm == 1; MM; MES; VPE; UMSCH_MM; ISP. Blocks registered before a failing helper stay registered. It returns 0 if all succeed.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_discovery.c:2559-3175 (checked 2559-3175). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the DIRECT/RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO SMU registration happens after SDMA (lines 3143-3153), and SMU for PSP load happens before display (3129-3137).

name: amdgpu_ring_init
prose: Precondition: adev, ring and ring->funcs are valid; max_dw, hw_prio and sched_score as used by the caller. Behaviour: it chooses sched_hw_submission (the module value, at least 256 for a KIQ ring, 8 for a MES ring, 256 for the first SDMA page ring). If ring->adev is NULL it returns -EINVAL if adev->num_rings is already AMDGPU_MAX_RINGS; otherwise it sets ring->adev, num_hw_submission and sched_score, assigns the next ring index, stores the ring in adev->rings, increments num_rings and calls amdgpu_fence_driver_init_ring (returning its error, after the ring was already registered). It then gets five writeback slots (rptr, wptr, fence, trail_fence, cond_exe) with amdgpu_device_wb_get, returning the first error and leaving the slots obtained so far allocated; it fills in the matching GPU/CPU addresses and sets the cond_exe value to 1. For a non-CPER ring it calls amdgpu_fence_driver_start_ring (error returned), computes the maximum IB dwords, raises max_dw with a WARN if it is too small and sets ring_size to roundup_pow_of_two(max_dw * 4 * sched_hw_submission); for a CPER ring it sets ring_size from max_dw * 4, count_dw and zeroes wptr and the rptr value, without starting the fence ring. It sets buf_mask, ptr_mask and cached_rptr = 0, allocates ring_backup if NULL (-ENOMEM on failure) and, if ring_obj is NULL, creates the ring buffer object in GTT with amdgpu_bo_create_kernel (on failure it frees ring_backup with kvfree, does not set the pointer to NULL, and returns the error) and clears it. It stores max_dw and hw_prio, takes a stub fence for vmid_wait and, unless ring->no_scheduler is set or the ring type is not below AMDGPU_HW_IP_NUM, appends &ring->sched to the gpu_sched list for its type and priority and increments num_scheds. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_ring.c:232-392. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: ring_backup is freed without being reset (line 374) and amdgpu_ring_fini (401-425) frees ring_backup again and never frees trail_fence_offs.

name: amdgpu_sdma_reset_engine
prose: Precondition: instance_id selects a valid SDMA instance of adev, and the caller does not hold that instance's engine_reset_mutex. Behaviour: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP without locking if adev is an SR-IOV VF. Otherwise it takes sdma_instance->engine_reset_mutex; if caller_handles_kernel_queues is false it stops the scheduler work queues of the instance's GFX ring and (when adev->sdma.has_page_queue) its page ring. If the instance has a stop_kernel_queue hook it calls it for the gfx ring and for the page ring when present. It calls amdgpu_sdma_soft_reset, which returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the instance has no soft_reset_kernel_queue hook; on failure it logs an error and skips restarting the queues, otherwise it calls the start_kernel_queue hook (if present) for the same rings. If caller_handles_kernel_queues is false and the reset succeeded it force-completes the rings' fences and restarts their scheduler work queues (on failure they stay stopped). It releases the mutex and returns the reset result (0 or a negative errno).
note: slice cut head; the real function is amdgpu_sdma_reset_engine(adev, instance_id, caller_handles_kernel_queues) at amdgpu_sdma.c:553-613, not amdgpu_sdma_reset_instance; the rings are derived inside from the instance.

name: NUM_SDMA

name: amdgpu_vcn_resume
prose: Precondition: i is a VCN instance index; for a non-harvested instance vcpu_bo is expected to be set, and when saved_bo is NULL the instance's fw must be non-NULL (its header is read even for a PSP load). Behaviour: it returns 0 without doing anything if the instance is harvested (bit i of harvest_config) and -EINVAL if vcpu_bo is NULL. If saved_bo is non-NULL it copies it into the VCPU buffer with memcpy_toio only if drm_dev_enter succeeds (paired with drm_dev_exit), then always kvfrees saved_bo and sets it to NULL. If saved_bo is NULL and the firmware load type is not PSP, it copies the ucode into the start of the buffer only when drm_dev_enter succeeds, then in all cases advances past the ucode size and zeroes only the remaining bytes with memset_io (the ucode region is left untouched when drm_dev_enter fails); if the load type is PSP it zeroes the whole buffer with memset_io. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_vcn.c:366-407. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: when drm_dev_enter fails for a non-PSP load only the bytes after the ucode are zeroed (lines 400-403); the memset_io is not guarded by drm_dev_enter.

name: amdgpu_vram_mgr_new
prose: Precondition: man, tbo, place and res are valid and the caller does not hold mgr->lock. Behaviour: it returns -ENOMEM if the amdgpu_vram_mgr_resource cannot be allocated; it initialises the TTM resource and, if ttm_resource_manager_usage(man) exceeds the usable VRAM size (mc_vram_size, minus AMDGPU_VM_RESERVED_VRAM for non-kernel BOs), it finalises the resource, frees it and returns -ENOSPC. It sets the buddy allocation flags from the placement and BO flags (top-down, contiguous, cleared, range) and, for a contiguous GFX12 DCC BO with a DCC alignment, enlarges the request. Under mgr->lock it allocates blocks with gpu_buddy_alloc_blocks in a loop; when a contiguous request fails with -ENOSPC and the place does not itself demand TTM_PL_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS (pages_per_block is ~0ul only for contiguous BOs) it clears the contiguous flag, lowers pages_per_block and retries; any other buddy error frees the allocated blocks, releases the lock, finalises the resource, frees it and returns that error. On success it records the current pid and comm, appends the resource to mgr->allocated_vres_list, optionally trims the DCC block, releases the lock, computes base.start and the visible usage from the blocks, sets TTM_PL_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS in the placement if the blocks are contiguous, sets the bus caching (cached for XGMI connected to the CPU, otherwise write-combined), adds the visible usage to mgr->vis_usage, stores the resource in *res and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_vram_mgr.c:442-625 (this tree uses gpu_buddy). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the retry also requires pages_per_block == ~0ul (line 547-548).

name: gfx_v10_0_rlc_resume
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device with the firmware load type and PSP autoload support determined. Behaviour: if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_PSP and psp.autoload_supported is set, it waits for the RLC autoload to complete (returning its error), initialises the clear-state buffer, sets the SPM vmid to 0xf and, unless the device is an SR-IOV VF, enables the RLC SRM, then returns 0. Otherwise, for an SR-IOV VF it only initialises the clear-state buffer and returns 0. For a non-VF it stops the RLC, writes 0 to the RLC CGCG/CGLS control register (clock gating off) and to RLC_PG_CNTL (power gating off), then loads the RLC microcode with gfx_v10_0_rlc_load_microcode if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT (returning its error) or enables backdoor autoload if it is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO (returning its error); other load types do neither. It then initialises the clear-state buffer, sets the SPM vmid to 0xf, starts the RLC, and, for AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO, waits for autoload completion (returning its error). It returns 0 otherwise.
note: slice cut head; function is gfx_v10_0.c:5567-5624. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this tree: the code writes mmRLC_CGCG_CGLS_CTRL and mmRLC_PG_CNTL (5593-5596); round 2 RIGHT (microcode load only for AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT).
